Subject: Dedicated sizing sprint handoff for ACME closes

Team + Sara,

Quick note to kick off a short sprint to lock dedicated sizing for the ACME Q4 closes. They sign a pilot on Dec 15 and want a 6-month committed pool. We need a clear sizing recommendation and the finance ask by Dec 3 so procurement can start the paperwork.

Agenda (15–20 min sync after replies):
- Confirm committed GPU slot count and expected token volumes
- Pricing anchor + finance caveats
- Infra readiness: canary plan + burst fallback
- Action owners and dates (procurement, infra, sales)

Attached: runway_sizing_model.csv (starter numbers). Please reply with: 1) recommended slot count and reason, 2) any infra blockers, 3) immediate finance asks.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: runway_sizing_model.csv (CSV - sizing inputs)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing sprint handoff for ACME closes

Thanks Camila — reviewed the CSV and sketched three scenarios quickly:

1) Conservative (baseline): 8 slots committed
   - Assumes prefix caching + 20% burst usage
   - Estimated monthly burn: ~120k tokens / slot-day equivalent; finance estimate attached

2) Performance (recommended): 12 slots committed
   - Low tail latency target; handles steady request rate + 30% headroom for marketing events

3) Aggressive (expansion): 18 slots committed
   - For customers expecting spikes and low-latency SLAs; higher unit cost but simpler routing

My recommendation is option 2 (12 slots) to balance cost and SLAs. If finance pushes back, we can include burst credits and a 60-day review clause.

Sending ACME anchor pricing and a simple cost model (attachment). I also flagged the Dec 15 commitment date so procurement timelines are visible.

Laura
Director, Sales Operations

Attachment: ACME_dedicated_pricing.xlsx (Excel - pricing anchors and cost model)

Appreciate the quick calc, Laura. A few finance notes:

- Option 2 (12 slots) looks reasonable as an initial committed base.
- We need the expected token burn by week (not just monthly) to model cashflow and discounting for a 6-month term. Laura, can you add a weekly burn curve to the spreadsheet?
- Proposal for commercial: 6-month commit, 10% prepay discount if they prepay 3 months upfront. That preserves runway for fleet procurement.
- Securitize PO timeline: procurement typically needs 10 business days once pricing is confirmed. procurement@altura.com, please confirm if that's workable.

I attached a short finance view (one-sheet) with recommended billing milestones and a DocuSign template reference.

Ben
Sr. Revenue Operations Analyst

Folks — infra perspective:

- Current available pool (US region) can support a 12-slot commitment for the requested Dec 15 start if we reserve by Dec 5.
- Two cautions: 1) we have a provisioning freeze Dec 24–Jan 2 (holiday maintenance), 2) 3rd-party GPU lead times are spiky — if ACME wants guaranteed capacity beyond 6 months we should add a buffer or prioritized replenishment.

Operational mitigations:
- Canary: we can stand up a 2-slot canary for the first 2 weeks to validate latency/kv cache behavior. See attached canary_config_notes.pdf for a checklist.
- Burst: propose 30% burst credits for first 60 days (metered) to cover marketing spikes.
- Rollout plan: reserved pool -> canary -> full activation; we can do staged routing to reduce risk.

I'll slot infra to start reserving once procurement confirms the PO window.

Karthik
Head of Infra Operations

Attachment: canary_config_notes.pdf (PDF - infra canary checklist)

Thanks everyone — quick summary and action owners before we lock the PO: 

Decisions:
- Go with Performance option: 12 committed slots (Laura)
- Offer: 6-month commit, 10% prepay discount if ACME prepays 3 months (Ben)
- Infra: 2-slot canary + 30% burst credits for 60 days (Karthik)

Action items (owners / dates):
- Laura: update ACME_dedicated_pricing.xlsx with weekly burn curve and final anchor by 2025-12-01 EOD.
- Ben: finalize billing milestones + DocuSign template and share by 2025-12-01 EOD.
- Karthik: reserve the 12-slot pool (hold until PO) and prep canary playbook; confirm by 2025-12-05.
- Camila: confirm commercial terms with Sara/ACME and collect signed PO by 2025-12-10.
- procurement@altura.com: confirm the 10 business day window for PO processing.

Sara — can you confirm ACME is comfortable with the 6-month term + prepay option? If yes we’ll proceed to pull the PO timeline into procurement.

Meeting: if needed, 20-min sync on 2025-12-02 10:00 PST to finalize anchors.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Camila + team — thanks for the fast turnaround. ACME is comfortable with the 6-month term and the 10% prepay discount; Sara here, copied in procurement as requested. We should be able to get an internal PO to you by Dec 9, pending a final one-page SOW.

Couple of asks from our side:
- Can the canary period include a short SLA window for latency anomalies so we can validate production behaviour?
- Please include a simple rollback trigger in the SOW if latency/regression exceeds agreed thresholds in the first 14 days.

I’ll coordinate with procurement and circle back with a PO ETA.

Best,
Sara
Head of Product — Acme Corp
